I have farmed this 10.1 mu of land in Quzhou County for 40 years. I am 55 now and I finished middle school. My wife and I live here. My son works in a factory in Shijiazhuang and sends money home, but the farm still needs to pay for itself.

Right now it is April and my winter wheat is turning green in the field. I planted it last October after the maize harvest. I used an improved wheat variety — I bought the seed from the agricultural supply shop in town, about 30 jin per mu. Before sowing, I plowed the field and put down base fertilizer: one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu, the 15-15-15 type. Now at jointing time, I will top-dress with about 20 kg of urea per mu. In total that comes to about 18 kg of nitrogen, 7 kg of phosphorus, and 7 kg of potassium per mu for the wheat. Some neighbors put more nitrogen, but Lao Wang uses about the same and he got 500 kg per mu last year, so I copy him. I will irrigate three times for this wheat: once before winter, once now at jointing, and once at heading in May. I already sprayed herbicide once in March, and I will spray one more time if I see aphids or rust. I expect about 500 kg per mu.

After wheat harvest in early June, I will immediately plant hybrid maize. There is no time to waste — I use rotary tillage right after the combine leaves, then sow. I buy hybrid seed, about 3 kg per mu. For fertilizer, I put 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base, and at the big trumpet stage in July I spread 20 kg of urea. That is about 15 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice: once at trumpet stage in July, and once in August during grain filling. I spray pesticide twice — once for corn borer and once depending on what insects show up. I expect about 580 kg per mu.

I learned all this from doing it year after year and watching what works on my neighbors' fields. I do not trust outside advice unless I saw it work with my own eyes. Fertilizer is expensive now — urea is over 100 yuan per bag — but I would rather apply a bit too much than risk losing yield. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. Last year was decent, so I will do the same this year. My son's off-farm income helps when I need to hire the combine or buy inputs, but I still count every yuan carefully.
